problem:
Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{\sqrt{3}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Region

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/22058df7ac75e085e1dc352736d1abf289e80d68f340ee63687e69d18e9b23c2.png)

Evaluate ${\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{y}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}\,dx\,dy\,dz.$ The region of integration is shown above.

*Hint: Change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We cannot integrate the given integral because we cannot find a simple antiderivative of the integrand. So, we change the order of integration.

We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(z),$ ${v}_{2}(z),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{y}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}\,dx\,dy\,dz={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le \pi ,\,\,0\le y\le \pi ,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

The region $R$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/c5eec166cdce2fa4be756aa144b6a802082def0374c2b6150794cb2f0f22f1a6.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type II *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/50a93024f817970869a3dcef831abc2515fe14efac5ec9dd778701d063b8351d.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x.
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\pi .
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,x\le y\le \pi },
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/ec3bc5a58b5521286388294b97e1449bb41548004477d6d4555c9b7b917f2bd7.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve given by $x=\pi .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/205c88cdd0b8a2676bc8396760095fa238ae39acd3660ed5aba2df3726161410.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \pi ,\,\,0\le z\le \pi }.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{y}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{x}^{\pi }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}\,dy\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}[{\int }_{x}^{\pi }\text{d}y]\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}[y]_{x}^{\pi }\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\pi -x}\cdot (\pi -x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi }\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-(-1-1)\,\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\text{d}z \\  & =2[z]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
